'''''Ceramium''''' is a [[genus]] of red algae (or [[Red algae|Rhodophyta]]). It is a large genus with at least 15 [[species]] in the [[British Isles]].<ref name="Maggs 93">''Maggs, C.A. and Hommersand, M.H.'' 1993. ''Seaweeds of the British Isles. vol.'''1''', Rhodophyta Part 3A Ceramiales.'' HMSO & Natural History Museum, London. {{ISBN|0-11-310045-0}}</ref>

The fully [[corticate]]d group previously referred to as ''Ceramium rubrum'', an illegitimate name, is represented, in the British Isles by: ''[[Ceramium pallidum]],'' ''Ceramium botryocarpum'', ''Ceramium nodulosum'' and ''Ceramium secundatum''.<ref name="Maggs 93"/><ref name="Morton">Morton, O. 1994. ''Marine Algae of Northern Ireland.'' Ulster Museum. {{ISBN|0-900761-28-8}}</ref>

==Description==
All species of ''Ceramium'' are small algae growing to no more than 30 cm (12 in) in length. They consist of a terete [[monosiphonous algae|monosiphonous]]<ref>Newton, L. 1931. ''A Handbook of the British Seaweeds''. British Museum (Natural History)</ref> axis of [[Cell (biology)|cells]] surrounded by smaller cells forming a [[wikt:cortex|cortex]]. In most species this a continuous cortex enclosing the axis, in others the cortical cells are arranged only in nodes at the junction of cells of the axes. The tips of the branches grow in a  pincer-like manner.<ref>Bunker, F.StP.D. Maggs, C.A. Brodie, J.A. and Bunker, A.R. 2017 ''Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland. Second Edition,'' Wild Nature Press, Plymouth, UK {{ISBN|978-0-9955673-3-7}}</ref> Species in the genus show irregular branching and are attached by unicellular or branched [[rhizoids]].<ref name="Maggs 93"/>

==Reproduction==
The species is [[dioecious]] forming [[spermatangia]] and carpogonia on separate male and female plants. The fertilised [[carpogonium]] develops growing parasitically attached to the female plant. Tetraspores are born in the cortical bands.<ref name="Maggs 93"/>

==Distribution==
[[File:Red alga Ceramium tenuicorne.jpg|thumb|''[[Ceramium tenuicorne]]'' under epifluorescence microscope]]

===British Isles===
[[Scotland]]: [[Orkney]] and [[Faroes]], [[Shetland]], [[Ross and Cromarty]], [[Fife]].<ref name="Maggs 93"/> 
England and Wales: Pembroke, Hampshire, Dorset, Devon and Cornwall, Sussex, Lincoln to Kent, Norfolk also the Channel Isles.
[[Ireland]]: Cork, Kerry, Clare, Mayo, Waterford, Dublin, Donegal,<ref>Morton, O. 2003. The marine macroalgae of County Donegal, Ireland. ''Bulletin of the Irish Biogeographical Society'' '''27''':3 - 164</ref> Antrim and Down.<ref name="Maggs 93"/><ref name="Morton"/>

===World===
Some species are probably cosmopolitan. Widely in north-west Atlantic, Iceland, Norway to Spain, Denmark, Netherlands, France, Portugal, Mediterranean, Azores, Canary Islands, Cape Verde Islands, USA - Newfoundland to New York, Australia.<ref name="Maggs 93"/>
